title: Page
description: The numbers and the table of widths of a workbook's page, format/page.yaml (section 14 of the format text): canvas lays every page out by them, and task.workbook-page holds every task on a workbook to them. Units are those of the page, and a width of a character is in whole hundredths of the type size.

sheet.description: The page, as large as the handwriting sheet.

numbers.description: The numbers of the layout, in units of the page.

most_items.description: The most items that a page holds, 99 at most: the column of their numbers is two digits and a full stop wide.

widths.description: The table of widths, in whole hundredths of the type size.

joints.description: The marks that glue two neighbours of a line together.

width.description: The width of the page, in its units.

height.description: The height of the page, in its units.

page_sheet.description: The page, as large as the handwriting sheet.

size.description: The type size of the text of a line.

box_width.description: The width of a box, the same for every box of the task.

line.description: The height of a line of text without a box.

lead.description: Between a line with a box and one without, in an item that wraps.

gap.description: Between a box and a word beside it, and between an item's number and its line.

apart.description: Between two boxes side by side, and between two lines with boxes in an item that wraps.

gutter.description: Between the two columns of short items.

margin.description: The margin of the page on its sides, its top and its bottom.

page_numbers.description: The numbers of the layout, in units of the page.

code_point.description: The code point of the space, U+ and four to six hexadecimal digits.

page_space_width.description: A space that does not break, of its own width.

width.description: The width of such a character, a square.

items.description: A code point, or a range of them.

ranges.description: The ranges of the wide characters.

page_wide.description: The characters of a square's width: Hangul, CJK, the full-width forms and emoji.

digits.description: The digits, all of one width.

signs.description: The signs of operations and comparisons, all of one width.

space.description: The space between two words, which the layout sets itself.

characters.description: The characters of a width of their own, each class by its width.

items.description: A space that does not break, of its own width.

spaces.description: The spaces that do not break, each a character of its word.

items.description: A code point, or a range of them, U+…–U+….

zero.description: The code points of no width, each joining the character before it.

wide.description: The characters of a square's width: Hangul, CJK, the full-width forms and emoji.

items.description: A code point of white space that breaks.

breaks.description: The white space that a line breaks at: a run of it is one space between two words, and none at the ends of a piece.

unknown.description: The width of a character that the table does not know.

joiner.description: The joiner: the code point after it goes with the one before it.

regional_indicators.description: The regional indicators, two of which make a flag, one cluster.

page_widths.description: The table of widths, in whole hundredths of the type size.

closing.description: The marks that a word glues to the word before it: no space between them, and no break.

opening.description: The marks that glue a word to the word after it, or to a box: no break after them.

page_joints.description: The marks that glue two neighbours of a line together.
